documents.title: Doc 75 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - Technical infringement
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - Technical infringement

details.fact: The rear diffuser of Car 6 was found to be lower than the minimum height stipulated in Article 3.4.1a of the 2026 FIA F3 Technical Regulations.
details.infringement: Article 3.4.1.a of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Championship Technical Regulations.
details.decision: Disqualification of Car 6 from the Classification of Race 2 (Feature). All cars originally classified behind Car 6 are moved up one place in the Race classification. All lap times set by Car 6 during the Race are cancelled.
details.reason: The Stewards, having received the report of the Technical Delegate (Document 57), summoned (Document 62) and heard the driver of Car 6 (De Palo), the Team Representative and the Race Engineer. The Technical Delegate reported that, following Race 2, the diffuser of Car 6 was found to be below the minimum height required by Article 3.4.1.a of the FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations. After the 5 mm tolerance under Article 3.4.2 had been taken into account, the diffuser measured up to 3 mm below the minimum on the right-hand side and 1 mm below the minimum on the left-hand side. The Team Representative confirmed the measurements taken by the Technical Delegate. The team submitted, however, that Car 6 had received a number of rear impacts from Car 5 (Slater), the Driver's team-mate, during Race 2, most likely in the diffuser area, and invited the Stewards to review the footage in support of that account. The Stewards reviewed the footage of the final two laps of Race 2 and confirmed that Car 5 made contact with Car 6 on two occasions during that period. The Stewards and the Technical Delegate inspected Car 5 and observed some damage to its front wing. On inspection of Car 6, the Stewards observed only very minimal scratches to the rear diffuser. The Race Engineer stated his belief that the contact from Car 5 may have caused a deformation or bending of the diffuser plates. Article 11.7.3 of the ISC provides that, where the regulations place the burden of proof on the person alleged to have committed a breach, that person must satisfy the Stewards, on the balance of probability, that the fact asserted is more likely than not to be true. Under Article 1.4 of the Technical Regulations, the car must comply with the FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations in their entirety at all times during a Competition, and under Article 1.8 it is the duty of the Competitor to satisfy the Technical Delegate and the Stewards that its car so complies. The burden of establishing compliance therefore rests, at all times, with the Competitor. The longstanding jurisprudence of the FIA International Court of Appeal (the "ICA") holds that a breach of the technical regulations must lead to disqualification unless the Competitor has committed no fault, whether intentionally or through negligence, and the non-conformity is the result of exceptional circumstances. These two conditions are cumulative, and exceptional circumstances are admitted only under very limited criteria. The ICA has likewise declined to accept an in-race incident as the cause of a technical irregularity where the physical condition of the car does not support that account (ICA-2014-03). Applying that framework, the breach is established and is not disputed. The Team Representative confirmed the measurements, and the Stewards are comfortably satisfied that the diffuser of Car 6 was below the minimum height permitted by Article 3.4.1.a after the applicable tolerance. The burden then rests on the Competitor to show, on the balance of probability, that the car was compliant before the contact and that the contact from Car 5 caused the non-conformity. The Stewards considered whether the contact from Car 5 was, by itself, enough to relieve the Competitor of the consequence of the non-conformity. The Stewards accepted that contact occurred twice. The burden, however, was on the Competitor to show that it was more likely than not that the contact caused the non-conformity, and the Competitor produced nothing to meet it. Beyond the assertion that the contact may have deformed the diffuser, no evidence was put before the Stewards connecting the contact to the measurements found. The very minimal scratches observed on Car 6 showed no breakage consistent with a displacing impact. The Technical Delegate confirms that the diffuser assembly was properly fixed and they did not note any displacement or misalignment. With no evidence before them capable of tipping the balance of probability in the Competitor's favour, the Stewards cannot treat the contacts as the cause of the breach. The Competitor has therefore not met the burden upon it. In-race contact of this nature does not meet the strict and narrow criteria for exceptional circumstances recognized by the International Court of Appeal. For these reasons, and having considered the matters raised extensively, the Stewards find that Car 6 is in breach of Article 3.4.1.a of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Championship Technical Regulations, and that the Competitor has not provided evidence capable of relieving it of its obligation to ensure the conformity of the car. The Stewards therefore issue the disqualification as a standard penalty for a technical infringement.

documents.title: Doc 67 - DECISION - Car 21 - Allegedly left the track and gained an advantage
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 21 - Allegedly left the track and gained an advantage

details.fact: Car 21 (Wharton) left the track at Turn 6 and gained a lasting advantage over Car 27 (David)
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations Alleged Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (c) of the FIA International Sporting Code
details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards examined the video evidence, summoned (Documents 53 & 54), and heard from the Drivers of Car 21 (Wharton) and Car 27 (David). On the approach to Turn 6, Car 27 was on the left (inside) and Car 21 on the right, with Car 21 attempting to pass around the outside of the corner. Car 27 stated that he was ahead of Car 21 at the apex of Turn 6 and was defending an outside overtake attempt. He stated that, in accordance with the F2/F3 Driving Standards Guidelines, Car 21 did not earn entitlement to the corner. Car 21 stated that he had the sufficient overlap (his front axle was ahead of Car 27’s front axle) to be entitled to racing room, and that the lack of room left by Car 27 forced him wide. He stated that he remained in full control of the car throughout the corner and was not aware that he had exceeded track limits due to the close proximity of the two cars. He added that, had he been aware he had left the track, he would have given the position back. Having considered the mater extensively, the Stewards were unable to definitely conclude, with sufficient clarity, the relative position of both cars at the apex of the corner. Accordingly, the Stewards decide to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 65 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 9 - Failing to follow RD instructions - Weaving
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 9 - Failing to follow RD instructions - Weaving

details.fact: Car 9 (Giusti) was weaving after the Bridge between Turn 14 and 15 in contravention to the Race Director’s Competition Notes.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.i. of the International Sporting Code (failure to follow Item 10.4 of the Race Director’s Competition Notes)
details.decision: Five (5) seconds time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (a) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations. There are no penalty points associated with this penalty.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned (Document 60) and heard from Driver of Car 9 (Giusti) and the Team Representative. During the Team Managers and Driver Meeting the Race Director gave instructions to all drivers that weaving is not permitted after the bridge between Turn 14 and Turn 15 until the driver passes the control line. This was to reduce and mitigate the risk(s) of incident(s) at the restart following a Safety Car period, The Stewards determined that Car 9 (Giusti) was weaving after the bridge approaching Turn 15. The Driver apologized for his lapse in judgement. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards view that in addition to the safety aspects of these instructions, a sporting advantage is also gained by a car warming up its tires after the aforementioned bridge. The Stewards impose a five (5) seconds time penalty in line with previous precedents.

documents.title: Doc 48 - DECISION - Car 27 - Allegedly forced Car 6 off track
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 27 - Allegedly forced Car 6 off track

details.fact: Car 27 (David) was alleged to have forced Car 6 (De Palo) off track at Turn 15.
details.infringement: Alleged Breach of Appendix L Chapter IV Article 2 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code
details.decision: No Further Action
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed the video evidence, summoned (Documents 45 & 46), and heard from the Drivers of Car 27 (David) and Car 6 (De Palo), together with their Team Representatives. On the approach to Turn 15, Car 27 was on the right (inside) and Car 6 on the left (outside), running side by side through the corner. The Driver of Car 27 stated that he was defending his position on the final lap of the race. Whilst aware that Car 6 was attempting to overtake, he maintained that Car 6 had not satisfied the criteria under the F2/F3 Driving Standards Guidelines for an outside overtake, and had therefore not earned the right to room at the exit of Turn 15. The Driver of Car 6 stated that, having gained a strong run under DRS, he drew alongside Car 27 and attempted to pass around the outside of Turn 15. He contended that Car 27 was carrying too much speed into the corner and had no proper means of defending his position at the exit. The F2/F3 Driving Standards Guidelines provide that, to be entitled to room (including at the exit) when overtaking on the outside of a corner, the overtaking car must: "have its front axle ahead of the front axle of the other car at the apex". The Stewards further note that overtaking on the outside of a high-speed corner carries an inherently greater level of risk, and the overtaking car must be ahead at the apex to establish entitlement to racing room. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that Car 6 was alongside, but not ahead of, Car 27 through the whole corner, and accordingly did not satisfy the criteria required to earn priority at the exit. As the obligation under the Guidelines to earn priority rests with the overtaking car, and Car 6 had not met that standard, the right to the corner remained with Car 27 as the defending car, and Car 6 was not forced off by Car 27. Accordingly, the Stewards decide to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 33 - INFRINGEMENT - ART Grand Prix - Unsafe act
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - ART Grand Prix - Unsafe act

details.fact: ART Grand Prix guests were standing in a potentially unsafe location in pit lane during the Qualifying Session.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: A fine of 2000 Euros to be paid by the Team. In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the ISC, fines shall be paid within forty‐eight hours of their notification by means of bank transfer to the FIA.
details.reason: The Stewards having reviewed video evidence, summoned (Document 31) and heard the Team Representative. The Stewards received a Marshal report through the Race Director, stating that two (2) guests of ART Grand Prix were in the working lane of the Pit Lane during the Qualifying Session. The Team Representative, having been given the opportunity to check with the team to confirm the identity and affiliation with the guests, confirmed that they were in fact team guests. He apologized for the situation and for the lapse in judgement. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards considered that team guests were watching the Qualifying Session from an unsafe location rather than behind the barriers. In light of these facts, the Stewards determined that the location of the guests created a potentially unsafe situation and may have put the guests at risk. The Stewards therefore elect that the appropriate penalty (a team fine), is in line with previous precedents.

documents.title: Doc 30 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 23 - Pit lane infringement
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 23 - Pit lane infringement

details.fact: Driver of Car 23 (Shin) failed to stop at the red light at the end of pit exit
details.infringement: Breach of Article 31.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations
details.decision: A drop of three grid positions for both the Sprint and Feature Races at this Competition. In addition, 2 penalty points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 4 points.
details.reason: The Stewards having reviewed video footage and positioning/marshalling system data, summoned (Document 25) and heard the Driver of Car 23 (Shin) and the Team Representative. The Driver of Car 23 entered the F1 Pit Lane, erroneously, after failing to follow Race Director’s Instructions (Document 29). The Driver reached the end of the F1 Pit Lane and failed to stop at the red light. The Driver stated that, he was facing communication issues and was not able to talk to his team via radio. He stated, after having failed to enter the correct pit lane, that he did not observe the red light at the pit exit and left the pit exit to return to the Support Pit Lane. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that the Driver failed to stop at the red light at the pit exit and is found to be in breach of Article 31.3 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Championship Sporting Regulations. The Stewards therefore impose a three (3) position grid drop for both the Sprint and the Feature Races in line with the Formula 3 Penalty Guidelines, and further assess two (2) Penalty Points for this infringement.

documents.title: Doc 29 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 23 - Failure to follow RD instructions - Support pit lane infringement
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 23 - Failure to follow RD instructions - Support pit lane infringement

details.fact: Car 23 (Shin) failed to directly return to the support pit lane after the session.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code and item 25.2 of the Race Director's Competition Notes.
details.decision: Reprimand (non-driving) to the Driver of Car 23. This is the driver's first Reprimand of the 2026 Season.
details.reason: The Stewards having reviewed video footage and positioning/marshalling system data, summoned (Document 24) and heard the Driver of Car 23 (Shin) and the Team Representative. At the end of the Qualifying Session, Driver of Car 23 was reported to have passed the chequered flag and instead of entering the Support Pit Lane, he continued the full lap and entered to the F1 Pit Lane. The driver stated that, after crossing the Finish Line, he was looking at his steering wheel and consequently failed to observe the chequered flag. He further stated that he immediately contacted the team by radio, after realizing his lapse, and he did not receive a response due to technical issues with his radio system. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that the driver failed to comply with item 25.1 of the Race Director's Event Notes by not returning to the support pit lane after the chequered flag. The Stewards therefore impose the standard penalty of a Reprimand (Non-Driving) in line with previous precents.

details.fact: A member of Car 19's (Rodin Motorsport) team personnel was wearing short trousers in the Working Area of the Pit Lane during the Practice Session

details.decision: A fine of 500 Euros to be paid by the Competitor. In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the ISC, fines shall be paid within forty‐eight hours of their notification by means of bank transfer to the FIA.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence and summoned and heard the team representative (document 11). Video evidence showed that a member of the teams personnel was wearing short trousers during the session. The team representative confirmed that the team member was wearing shorts and that he forgot to wear long trousers as stipulated in Article 22.15 of the Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that the team member did not comply with the aforementioned article and therefore impose a fine of 500 Euros to the team in line with previous precents.

documents.title: Doc 16 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 5 - Technical infringement
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 5 - Technical infringement

details.fact: Car 5 (Slater) was not able to provide a fuel sample of a minimum of 0.8 kg after the Practice Session.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 6.3.1 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations.
details.decision: Disqualification of Car 5 from the results of the Practice Session. Removal of all times set by Car 5 in the Practice Session. All cars originally classified behind Car 5 are moved up one place in the Practice Session classification.
details.reason: The Stewards received a report from the Technical Delegate (Document 10) and summoned the Driver and Team Representative (Document 12). The hearing was attended by the Team Representative. The Technical Delegate’s report indicated that they were unable to take the mandatory minimum fuel sample of 0.8kg from the Car at the end of the Practice Session. It is to be noted that Car 5 stopped on Track after completing its practice start. The Team Representative acknowledged that the minimum required fuel sample of 0.8 kg could not be taken from the Car at the end of the Practice Session. The Team Representative explained that this was due to the change in procedures during the running of the session, and that they had underestimated the fuel consumption required to run the session, VSC test and the practice start at the end of the session. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards acknowledge that the breach was a consequence of misjudgement. Nevertheless, the Stewards determine that the Competitor failed to comply with the requirements of Article 6.3.1 of the FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations and accordingly decide to disqualify Car 5 from the Practice Session.

documents.title: Doc 15 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 2 - Impeding of Car 9 in Practice
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 2 - Impeding of Car 9 in Practice

details.fact: Car 9 (Giusti) was impeded by Car 2 (Ugochukwu) who was driving slow on the racing line on the approach to Turn 6.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 31.6 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations Breach of Article 12.2.1.i. of the International Sporting Code (failure to follow Item 19 of the Race Director’s Competition Notes)
details.decision: Warning given to the Driver of Car 2.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the Drivers and Team representatives (Documents 13 and 14). Car 2 was on a cool-down lap on the approach to Turn 6 and was on the racing line. Car 9 was on a fast lap. Due to the speed differential, Car 9 had to overtake Car 2, and accordingly aborted his fast lap. Article 19 of the Race Director’s Competition Notes states: “When drivers are on the racing line, they must ensure that they are travelling at a speed sufficient to not unnecessarily impede any driver on or starting a fast lap.” In this case, Car 2 was driving slowly on the racing line. During the hearing the Driver of Car 2 acknowledged the mistake and apologised for the lapse. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determine that Car 2 unnecessarily impeded Car 9. The Stewards accordingly issue a warning in accordance with the penalty guidelines and in line with previous precedents for such infringements during the Practice Session.
